scope: Source and offline dataset audit only. The Pi is offline; installed software, motor gains, actual messages, acquisition timing and camera calibration have not been inspected.

input_contract.mapping: Named front-right joints 1,2,3 in position then velocity then published-effort order; no reordering by the SPI abad/hip/knee aliases.

expected_live_units.position: Joint angles in radians after local homing/sign/offset mapping; verify live zero conventions.
expected_live_units.velocity: Joint radians per second; verify firmware/installed driver scaling.
expected_live_units.effort: Published effort proxy in the driver PD convention; not sensor-measured torque. Dataset collection implementation and gains remain unidentified.

input_contract.first_pause_requirement: Two distinct predictions >=0.8; separate hysteresis/cooldown. This is not a calibrated end-to-end contact-detection latency bound.

findings.confirmed: Local C++ driver exports effort computed as Kp*(position_command-position_state)+Kd*(velocity_command-velocity_state). Receive struct supplies position, velocity and flags, not measured torque.
findings.implication: Preserve published values and verify provenance; substituting measured torque, zeros or another estimator changes the learned feature distribution. Historical CSV collection driver is unknown.

findings.confirmed: Local estimate omits feedforward effort, uses pre-clamping command/gain storage and does not model transport delay. Command-copy code separately clamps positions, velocities, effort and gains before SPI transmission.
findings.implication: Do not label the estimate as applied motor torque, calibrated load or electrical energy.

findings.confirmed: Hardware description declares position and velocity states for each joint, while driver also exports effort. ik.yaml sets a position-oriented broadcaster field; this is not proof of a published effort array.
findings.implication: Inspect installed ros2_control hardware interfaces, broadcaster parameters and actual JointState arrays. The adapter rejects missing effort; do not fill with zero. Exact runtime behavior depends on installed versions.

findings.confirmed: ik.py defines Kp=3 and Kd=.1 but publishes position targets only. The local driver sets gains during homing and leaves those command values afterward; local homing parameters are 5.5/.2. A separate gain controller could change them.
findings.implication: Record the active kp/kd/desired-velocity/feedforward ownership and values, rather than claiming the Python constants establish deployment gains. Do not infer historical dataset gains.

findings.confirmed: Adapter maps leg_front_r_1,2,3 by name. Hardware description maps them to CAN channel 2 IDs 1,2,3; SPI aliases are explicitly unrelated to anatomical joint names. State positions subtract homing zero after SPI sign/offset conversion.
findings.implication: No extra channel-order transform should be added. Verify physical front-right identity and same angle zero/sign convention on the robot.

findings.confirmed: Local IK controller-manager request is 1000 Hz; neural-controller stack requests 520 Hz with joint-state broadcaster 260 Hz. These are configuration requests, not measured sensor delivery rates. SPI joint receive fields have no per-sample acquisition timestamp.
findings.implication: Record header and receipt intervals, age, duplicates, gaps and actual array refresh. A 1,000 Hz interpolation grid does not create 1,000 Hz measurements. Historical CSV timestamp clock/source is unverified.

findings.confirmed: Optional Lab1 handout describes a DenseTact right-front foot experiment with tactile images at 3 Hz and a reference-based contact detector at 10 Hz. Explicit classifier consumes those tactile images, not front RGB images.

evidence.file: Course library: Optional Lab 1/Optional Lab 1 - Instructions.txt

findings.implication: No front-camera calibration can make the existing tactile classifier an RGB terrain recognizer. The live motor-only contact path does not require the tactile camera.

findings.confirmed: DenseTact collector/image_index exporter source was not supplied. Existing Gemini HTTP camera endpoint returns a cached JPEG without exposure/header timestamp; front camera intrinsics are fixed and lack camera-ID/resolution provenance.
findings.implication: For any new synchronized collection, capture actual ROS image header plus receipt clocks and verify resolution/intrinsics; do not align using HTTP request time or reuse front-camera frames as DenseTact input. Calibration validity is unverified, not proven wrong.

provided_dataset_provenance_limit: CSV effort channels are finite and nonzero in these recordings and timestamp intervals are approximately 1 ms. This establishes stored data content, not torque-sensor provenance, the historical driver revision or hardware sensing rate.

offline_shadow_validation.tests: implicit_compliance/tests plus foundation/tests/test_single_leg.py; includes fake subscription-only CLI, named-order mapping, missing/nonfinite efforts, gaps, duplicates/rewinds, stale/future timestamps and rate distinction.

actual_export_replay.scope: Offline interface replay of first 2,500 rows of a training recording with synthetic receipt clocks, not hardware timing or new accuracy evaluation.

next_live_trial.side_effects: Read-only ROS subscription and local log files; no motor publishers, services or controller launch.
capture: Installed ROS distro, ros2_control/broadcaster, hardware-interface and firmware revisions; actual effort array and active controllers.
kp/kd, feedforward and velocity command ownership/values; homing offsets/signs and physical right-front joint mapping.
Header clock and actual message rate, receipt age, gaps/duplicates, source freshness; sample-statistics comparison with training channels.
Actual Pi cold/warm inference latency, total callback load and thermals while existing stack runs.
Independent timestamped contact annotations on the intended trajectory, false triggers, misses and delays; no pause until calibration supports it.
next_live_trial.status: Live calibration remains required; source compatibility alone is not deployment approval.
